evidence_quotes.section1_opening: Rep jumps directly into address confirmation and logistics; no quid pro quo framing of time commitment or promise of dependable quote. No pause for customer agreement.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves straight into probing after address verification.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep states: 'for $2, that's gonna be $4,525... Earlier I quoted you like your $54,550 so but yeah, since we're doing it on a Sunday $105.' Pricing is given but anchor is unclear and not personalized to customer's move details.
evidence_quotes.two_promises: On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. No closing statement like 'Does that put those to rest?'
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'will there be anything else?' — a generic throwaway, not a genuine concerns check.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent. Moves directly to email confirmation and goodbye.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Date (Sunday Sept 27), time (2:00 PM), crew size (two movers, one truck), email confirmed. Missing: destination address (DK Ranch) fully spelled out, arrival window, and notes about customer concerns.

top_strength: Rep successfully retrieved customer from system, clarified a two-stop move (storage to house), and locked in a specific date/time with confirmed email contact.
coaching_note: This was a re-booking call, not a full sales call — you skipped Section 1 framing, never asked their agenda or two-layer concerns, gave no estimate anchor or Two Promises, and never asked for the business explicitly. Treat every inbound as a fresh sales call: open with quid pro quo, ask what's concerning them, deliver both promises, and close with an explicit ask before confirming details.
